n: God calls Cyrus His “anointed”—the only non-Israelite given this title. Cyrus wasn’t a believer, but God would use him to defeat kings and swing open city gates, as Babylon fell to him in 539 BC with little resistance.

f.g: Hebrew mashiaḥ (messiah)—one set apart for a special task.
Strip kings of their belts, i.e., disarm them.

n: God promises to go ahead of Cyrus, leveling obstacles and smashing gates of bronze and iron bars.
He will give Cyrus hidden treasures stored in dark vaults—Babylon and Lydia were famous for wealth. The purpose: so Cyrus would know the Lord who called him by name.

f.g: Riches hidden away in storerooms and vaults.

f.w: which call thee by thy name

n: All this is for Israel’s sake. God called Cyrus by name and gave him a title of honor, even though Cyrus didn’t know Him.
There is no God besides the Lord. He equipped Cyrus for battle even though Cyrus didn’t know Him—God works through people who don’t yet recognize Him.

f.g: Fastened your belt—prepared you for action.

n: The goal is for everyone from east to west to know there is no other God.
God is sovereign over everything—light and darkness, peace and calamity. Here “evil” means disaster or hardship, not moral wickedness. Even the rise and fall of empires is under His control.

f.g: Hebrew ra‘—trouble or calamity, the opposite of “peace” (shalom) in this line.

f.w: I form the light, and create darkness

n: A lovely image: let righteousness rain down from heaven and salvation sprout up from the earth. Latter-day Saints have linked this verse to the restoration—truth from heaven and the Book of Mormon from the earth.

f.w: let the earth open, and let them bring forth salvation

n: Woe to anyone who argues with his Maker—like a broken piece of pottery criticizing the potter, or clay saying, “What are you making?” or “You have no hands!”

f.w: Shall the clay say to him that fashioneth it

n: Or like a child scolding his parents for having him. Some Israelites may have resented God for using a pagan king to save them.
God, Israel’s Maker, says in effect: Do you question Me about My children, or tell Me how to do My work?

f.g: Probably ironic: “Would you give Me orders about My own work?”

n: He made the earth, created humanity, stretched out the heavens, and commands the stars. He has every right to direct history.
God raised Cyrus to rebuild His city and release His captives—not for a bribe or payment. Cyrus’s decree let exiles return and even funded the temple.

f.w: he shall let go my captives

n: A vision of nations coming to Israel—Egyptians, Cushites, and the tall Sabeans—acknowledging, “God is truly with you; there is no other.” The “chains” may suggest humble submission. Ultimately the nations turn to Israel’s God.

f.g: Tall people from Seba, probably in the Nile region or southern Arabia.

n: A cry of wonder: truly You are a God who hides Himself—working in hidden ways, even through a foreign king—yet You are Israel’s Savior.
Idol makers will all end in shame and confusion together.
But Israel will be saved by the Lord with an everlasting salvation and never be ashamed—forever.
God created the earth with a purpose—not to be empty, but to be inhabited. Latter-day Saints connect this to the plan of salvation: the earth was made as a home for God’s children.

f.w: he formed it to be inhabited

n: Unlike pagan oracles muttered in secret places, God has spoken openly. He never told Israel to seek Him for nothing; His words are true and right.

f.w: I have not spoken in secret

n: God invites survivors among the nations to gather and see: those who carry wooden idols and pray to gods that can’t save have no understanding.

f.w: ye that are escaped of the nations
f.g: Survivors from the nations, perhaps those left after Cyrus’s conquests.

n: Who predicted all this long ago? The Lord alone—a righteous God and a Savior. There is no one else.

f.w: a just God and a Saviour

n: One of the great gospel invitations: “Look to Me and be saved, all the ends of the earth.” Salvation is offered to every nation, not only Israel.

f.w: Look unto me, and be ye saved

n: God swears by Himself, since there is no one greater: every knee will bow and every tongue will confess Him. Paul applies this to Jesus Christ.
People will say, “Only in the Lord do I have righteousness and strength.” All will come to Him, and those who raged against Him will be ashamed.

f.w: in the LORD have I righteousness and strength

n: All Israel’s descendants will be justified—made right—in the Lord and will boast in Him, not in themselves.

f.g: Declared righteous, put right with God.
